args.notes: Bursty 8-channel sensor offload: bursts of 8 requests 0 ns apart, Poisson at 2 requests/us, p99 latency <= 0.4 us, err <= 2^-10, min LUTs+FFs. Prior campaign: iterative family dominated the front (data_width=15, n_iter=12, angle_guard=1, rounding=round won for a low-rate area-min spec); pipelined/pipelined_m/unrolled_k never reached a front. Cost model underestimates LUTs ~19%, FFs ~11%, Fmax ~10% low. For p99 latency, a single iterative CORDIC with ~12 iters at ~150 MHz is ~80 ns per request; 8 back-to-back requests = ~640 ns > 0.4 us p99 bound, so the system sim will likely need higher throughput (pipelined or unrolled) or a faster clock. Prioritize designs with enough throughput to drain 8-request bursts within 0.4 us p99, while keeping area low.

args.lesson: For bursty p99-latency CORDIC specs (bursts of 8, 2 req/us, p99 <= 0.4 us, err <= 2^-10, min LUTs+FFs), pipelined_m with m=4, data_width=15, n_iter=12, angle_guard=2, rounding=round wins (est 813 luts+ffs, 97.8 MSPS, simulated p99 0.135 us). Single-iteration iterative designs are too slow to drain 8-request bursts within p99; pipelined_m m=4 was the area/latency sweet spot. No L3/L4 measurements recorded for this design.
